Niche Construction — Organisms Shape Selection

From ecosystem engineering to cultural scaffolding: organisms change environments, which changes selection pressures — a feedback that reshapes evolution.

Traits, behaviours, technologies → Modified physical/social environment → New costs/benefits; altered risks → Gene freq. changes; cultural retention

Ecological Examples

Earthworms — Bioturbation aerates soil, mixes organics, changes pH → reshapes plant communities & soil biota; future worms evolve in altered soils.
Beavers — Dams create ponds/wetlands; shift hydrology, predator–prey dynamics, plant succession → selection on aquatic/semi-aquatic traits and behaviours.

Human Examples

Fire & Cooking — Landscape burning + cooked food alter calorie yield & pathogen load → implications for gut morphology, life history, sociality.
Agriculture — Sedentism, animal domestication, high-density living → novel disease ecologies; dairying → lactase persistence selection in multiple populations.
Technologies — Writing, schools, digital media create cognitive niches that shape attention, memory strategies, and cultural selection.

Why it Matters

Active agency: Organisms are not passive; they design parts of their own selective environment. Persistence: Modified niches can outlast individuals → ecological inheritance. Acceleration: Human cultural niches change faster than genes, yet feed back on biology.
